passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: ​ The following discussion should be read in conjunction with the audited consolidated financial statements of the Company and the notes thereto included in Item 18. Those consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards. ​ HISTORY ​ Ryanair’s current business strategy dates to the early 1990s, when Ryanair became the first European airline to replicate the low-fares, low-cost operating model pioneered by Southwest Airlines in the United States. During the period between 1992 and 1994, Ryanair expanded its route network to include scheduled passenger services between Dublin and Birmingham, Manchester and Glasgow (Prestwick). In 1994, Ryanair began standardizing its fleet by purchasing used Boeing 737-200A aircraft to replace substantially all of its leased aircraft. Beginning in 1996, Ryanair continued to expand its service from Dublin to new provincial destinations in the UK. Ryanair Holdings completed its initial public offering in June 1997. ​ From 1997 through March 31, 2026, the Ryanair Group launched services on approximately 2,200 routes and also increased the frequency of service on a number of its principal routes. Ryanair has established 95 airports as bases of operations. See “Item 4. Information on the Company—Route System, Scheduling and Fares” for a list of these bases. During FY19 and FY20 the Company established a low-cost airline group adding startup airlines in Poland (Buzz) and the UK (Ryanair UK), along with the acquisition of Lauda and Malta Air (both now based in Malta), to Ryanair DAC in Ireland. Ryanair has increased the number of booked passengers from approximately 5m in FY99 to over 208m in FY26. As of March 31, 2026, Ryanair had a principal fleet of 621 Boeing 737 (including 210 Boeing 737-8200 “Gamechangers”) aircraft and 26 Airbus A320 aircraft and serves approximately 235 airports. ​ 51 Table of Contents Ryanair expects to have approximately 800 narrow-body aircraft in its operating fleet by FY34 following the delivery of all of the Boeing 737s currently on order, subject to lease hand-backs and disposals over the period. See “Item 4. Information on the Company—Aircraft” and “Item 5. Operating and Financial Review and Prospects—Liquidity and Capital Resources” below for additional details. ​ BUSINESS OVERVIEW ​ Since Ryanair pioneered its low-cost operating model in Europe in the early 1990s, its passenger volumes and scheduled passenger revenues have increased significantly because the Company has substantially increased capacity and demand has been sufficient to match the increased capacity. Ryanair’s annual booked passenger volume has grown from approximately 1m passengers in 1991 to over 208m passengers in FY26. ​ Scheduled revenues rose 14% to €10.56bn as traffic grew 4% to over 208m passengers with 10% higher fares. Ancillary revenues delivered a solid performance, rising 6% to €4.99bn due to 4% traffic growth and 2% higher spend per passenger. ​ Ryanair’s total break-even load factor was 84% in FY25 and 80% in FY26. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: ​ Risks Related to the Company ​ The Company may not be successful in increasing fares to cover rising business costs. Ryanair operates a low-fares airline. The success of its business model depends on its ability to control costs so as to deliver low fares while at the same time earning a profit. Ryanair has limited control over its fuel costs and already has comparatively low operating costs. In periods of high fuel costs, if Ryanair is unable to further reduce its other operating costs or generate additional revenues, operating profits are likely to fall. Ryanair cannot offer any assurances regarding its future profitability. Changes in fuel costs and availability could have a material adverse impact on Ryanair’s results. See “—Changes in fuel costs and availability affect the Company’s results” and “—The Company faces significant price and other pressures in a highly competitive environment”. ​ Changes in fuel costs and availability affect the Company’s results. Jet fuel is subject to wide price fluctuations as a result of many economic and political factors and events occurring throughout the world that Ryanair can neither control nor accurately predict, including increases in demand, sudden disruptions in supply and other concerns about global supply, as well as market speculation. Oil prices increased significantly following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and remained volatile throughout 2022 and 2023. Most recently, oil prices increased significantly in March 2026 as a result of the conflict in Iran and broader escalation across the Middle East, which resulted in significant increases in jet fuel prices. In addition, there has been significant disruption to international shipping and trade routes through the Strait of Hormuz, through which approximately 20% of the world's oil and gas supply is typically transported, further exacerbating the impact on oil and jet fuel prices. A prolonged or escalating conflict in Iran and the Middle East has led and could continue to lead to a protracted period of uncertainty in the region and to increased volatility in and disruption to global energy markets, which could cause jet fuel prices to remain elevated or rise even higher. Moreover, even if the conflict in Iran subsides or terminates, there may be lasting disruptions to fuel production, including related infrastructure and transportation. Additionally, as international prices for jet fuel are denominated in U.S. dollars, Ryanair’s fuel costs are also subject to certain exchange rate risks. Substantial price increases, adverse exchange rates, or the unavailability of adequate fuel supplies, including, without limitation, any such events resulting from international terrorism, prolonged hostilities in the Middle East, Central and Eastern Europe, or other oil-producing regions or the further suspension of production by any significant producer, may adversely affect Ryanair’s profitability. credit_strengths.text: Ryanair's low-cost model and scale underpin strong operating cash generation, with operating cash flow comfortably exceeding capital expenditure and funding shareholder returns. This internally generated liquidity supports the airline's debt service and fleet investment without reliance on external financing, a key credit strength for an issuer with a minimal indicative financial risk profile.

The balance sheet is in a net cash position, with cash and cash equivalents exceeding reported borrowings. This provides a substantial liquidity buffer and limits refinancing risk, as the company can repay maturing debt from existing resources. The net cash position is a differentiator versus sector peers that typically carry positive net leverage.

key_risks.text: Ryanair's profitability is highly sensitive to jet fuel prices, which are subject to geopolitical shocks and exchange rate movements. The risk factor disclosure highlights recent oil price spikes and potential supply disruptions, which could compress margins if the company cannot pass through higher costs. This is a material earnings volatility risk for the credit.

The company's debt structure includes borrowings that may require refinancing, and while no specific maturity profile is disclosed, the reliance on debt markets could pose refinancing risk if credit conditions tighten. However, the net cash position and strong cash flow mitigate this risk, as internal funds can cover maturities.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is exceptionally strong, with operating income covering finance costs many times over. This provides a large cushion against earnings volatility and supports the company's ability to service debt even under stress. The coverage ratio is well above the sector median, reflecting the low absolute debt burden relative to earnings.

Free cash flow to debt is robust, indicating that the company generates sufficient cash after capital expenditure to repay a significant portion of its debt annually. This strong cash conversion supports debt servicing capacity and provides flexibility for shareholder returns and fleet investment without impairing credit quality.

overall_credit_view.text: Ryanair exhibits a minimal indicative financial risk profile, characterized by net cash, high interest coverage, and strong free cash flow. The company's low-cost model and scale provide competitive advantages, but fuel price volatility and competitive pressures remain key risks. The credit profile is supported by substantial liquidity and conservative debt levels.

The company's shareholder return program, including dividends and buybacks, absorbs a portion of free cash flow but remains comfortably covered by operating cash generation. While this reduces absolute liquidity build, the net cash position and strong coverage metrics provide ample headroom. The credit outlook is stable, contingent on fuel cost management and demand resilience.

credit_strengths.text: Ryanair的低成本模式與規模支撐強勁的營運現金生成，營運現金流舒適地超過資本支出及股東回報資金。此內部產生的流動性支持該航空公司的債務償付及機隊投資，無需依賴外部融資，對於具有最低指示性財務風險狀況的發行人而言是一項關鍵信用優勢。
資產負債表處於淨現金狀況，現金及現金等價物超過報告借款。這提供了可觀的流動性緩衝並限制了再融資風險，因為公司可從現有資源償還到期債務。淨現金狀況是相對於通常持有正淨槓桿的行業同行的差異化因素。

key_risks.text: Ryanair的盈利能力對航空燃油價格高度敏感，而燃油價格受地緣政治衝擊及匯率變動影響。風險因素披露強調了近期的油價飆升及潛在供應中斷，若公司無法轉嫁更高成本，可能壓縮利潤率。這是該信用的一項重大盈利波動風險。
公司的債務結構包括可能需要再融資的借款，雖然未披露具體到期情況，但若信用狀況收緊，對債務市場的依賴可能構成再融資風險。然而，淨現金狀況及強勁現金流緩解了此風險，因為內部資金可覆蓋到期債務。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率異常強勁，營運收入覆蓋財務成本多倍。這為盈利波動提供了巨大緩衝，並支持公司在壓力下償付債務的能力。覆蓋率遠高於行業中位數，反映相對於盈利的絕對債務負擔較低。
自由現金流對債務比率穩健，表明公司在資本支出後產生足夠現金，每年可償還其債務的顯著部分。此強勁的現金轉換支持債務償付能力，並為股東回報及機隊投資提供靈活性，而不損害信用質量。

overall_credit_view.text: Ryanair展現最低指示性財務風險狀況，其特點為淨現金、高利息覆蓋率及強勁自由現金流。公司的低成本模式與規模提供競爭優勢，但燃油價格波動及競爭壓力仍是關鍵風險。信用狀況得到大量流動性及保守債務水平的支持。
公司的股東回報計劃，包括股息及回購，吸收了部分自由現金流，但仍被營運現金生成舒適覆蓋。雖然這減少了絕對流動性積累，但淨現金狀況及強勁覆蓋指標提供了充足空間。信用展望穩定，取決於燃油成本管理及需求韌性。
